auditDuty: Rule 4(15), Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 (as amended): every e-commerce entity shall undertake a self-audit to identify and remove dark patterns from its platform.

BASKET_SNEAKING.framework: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 — Annex on dark patterns, Schedule item: Basket sneaking
BASKET_SNEAKING.plainBasis: Adding paid items, add-ons, or subscriptions to a cart or order by default, without the consumer's affirmative action, is listed as a prohibited dark pattern.

FALSE_URGENCY.framework: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 — Annex on dark patterns, Schedule item: False urgency
FALSE_URGENCY.plainBasis: Creating a sense of urgency or scarcity that is not genuine, such as fake countdown timers, is listed as a prohibited dark pattern.

INTERFACE_INTERFERENCE.framework: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 — Annex on dark patterns, Schedule item: Interface interference
INTERFACE_INTERFERENCE.plainBasis: Visually obscuring, de-emphasising, or otherwise making it harder for a consumer to find or exercise a choice they are entitled to make is listed as a prohibited dark pattern.

DRIP_PRICING.framework: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 — Annex on dark patterns, Schedule item: Drip pricing
DRIP_PRICING.plainBasis: Not disclosing mandatory, non-optional charges to the consumer in advance, and revealing them only at a later stage of the checkout flow, is listed as a prohibited dark pattern.

CONFIRM_SHAMING.framework: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 — Annex on dark patterns, Schedule item: Confirm shaming
CONFIRM_SHAMING.plainBasis: Using language and design choices to shame a consumer into opting into something, or making decline options read as an admission of a negative trait, is listed as a prohibited dark pattern.
